reasons: Handles bad server replies and network failures with messages.
The server-side checks for the invite and password are not shown in this file.

terms.meaning: the app accepts new accounts only when someone already holds a valid invite code
a web address the server answers, such as /api/auth/register
a reusable building block that draws one part of a web page
values a component remembers while it is on screen, such as what has been typed

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and client marker
sections.what: Brings in the React tools for remembering values, reading the page address and moving between pages, plus the link component. The first line marks this page to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form reacts to typing, which only happens in the browser.

sections.name: RegisterForm (part 1)
sections.title: Form memory and sign-up request
sections.what: Holds the typed values, the error text and the loading flag. It fills the invite code from the link, sends the sign-up request, and moves the user to the home page on success or shows the error. It also opens the page layout with the invite-only notice and the error box.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form must remember input and handle the server reply without reloading the page.
sections.watch_out: Error text is shown only if the server reply includes an error field, so the server must send one.

sections.name: RegisterForm (part 2)
sections.title: Input fields and submit button
sections.what: Draws the invite code, email and password boxes and the create account button. The button is disabled while the request runs. A sign-in link sits at the bottom.
sections.why: Likely reason: the browser checks required fields and the minimum password length before the request is sent.
sections.watch_out: The invite code is forced to capitals on screen and in the saved value, so the server must match codes without regard to case.

sections.name: RegisterPage
sections.title: Page wrapper and loading screen
sections.what: Exports the page visitors load. It wraps the form in a loading placeholder that shows LOADING briefly while the page address is read.
sections.why: Likely reason: reading the page address needs the Suspense wrapper that Next.js expects.
sections.watch_out: Removing this wrapper can break the page when it reads the invite code from the address.

summary: Sign-up page where a new user enters an invite code, email and password to create an account.
purpose: Lets someone who holds a valid invite create an account, because the app is invite-only.
why: Likely reason: the app is closed to the public, so the owner hands out codes to control who can join.
how: 1. Reads an optional invite code from the page address and fills it into the form in capital letters. 2. The user types the invite code, email and password. 3. On submit, the page sends them to the `/api/auth/register` route. 4. On success it moves the user to the home page and refreshes it. 5. On failure it shows the server's error text, or a network error message.
inputs: Invite code, email and password typed by the user, and an optional invite value from the page address.
outputs: A sign-up request to the server, then either a redirect to the home page or an error message on screen.
risks: The invite check happens on the server, not in this file, so this page alone does not stop bad codes. The 8-character password minimum is enforced only by the browser field, so the server must check it too (not visible here).
debug: If sign-up fails, read the error text on screen, then check the `/api/auth/register` route. If the invite code does not fill in from the link, check that the link uses the invite parameter. If the button does nothing, check the browser console for network errors.
